assertions: Offers two or three candidate one-liners for the point, rather than one
Names the reader: who they are, what they believe now, what should change

Marks turning points as what the reader should see or do, not how to build a visual
Includes honesty beats (what isn't solved or what went wrong first)

Flags that the rename behaviour needs confirming (reproduction steps or version) before publishing
Shows what at least two candidate phrasings of the point would each include or leave out
Leaves the brief unlocked and runs (or explicitly defers until the wording is chosen) a check of every beat against the point's wording
